success_criteria_results.criterion: Fix 1 - Slug extraction uses PLAN_DATE-based suffix removal
success_criteria_results.verification_method: Read script line 49; confirmed pattern is ${BASE_FILENAME%-${PLAN_DATE}}
success_criteria_results.details: Line 49 reads: DESTINATION_SLUG="${BASE_FILENAME%-${PLAN_DATE}}". For input 'new-york-city-2026-03-15', PLAN_DATE='2026-03-15', BASE_FILENAME='new-york-city-2026-03-15', so ${BASE_FILENAME%-2026-03-15} = 'new-york-city'. This is correct and avoids the old bug where ${BASE_FILENAME%-*} would strip at the first hyphen-digit boundary.

success_criteria_results.criterion: Fix 2 - Date fallback uses file modification time
success_criteria_results.verification_method: Read script line 62; confirmed pattern is $(date -r "$INPUT_FILE" +%Y-%m-%d)
success_criteria_results.details: Line 62 reads: PLAN_DATE=$(date -r "$INPUT_FILE" +%Y-%m-%d). This uses the file's modification time instead of current date, ensuring re-deployment of the same file produces the same date. This is idempotent behavior.
evidence: Local deployment confirms: china-feb-15-mar-7-2026 has date 2026-02-12 (file mod time), not today's date

However, the script structure ensures the variable is only accessed after being checked, and bash -u only triggers on actual expansion, so this is safe because line 216 is inside an if-block that checks -n first.
